scenarios.prompt: Our voice agent cuts callers off while they read a phone number. Its only turn rule is 500 ms of silence. Explain the likely failure and what to measure before changing the rule. Name the skill you used.

required.why: Separates VAD from end of turn
Names a turn detector as the fix direction

forbidden.why: Must not drop min endpointing below 0.3 s
Must not fix it by only raising the silence timeout

criteria: Selects turn-taking and reads bundled guidance
Tests digit pauses and uses measurements to justify changes

examples.pass: Skill: voice-turn-taking. VAD only knows audio went quiet; a phone number has pauses. Put a semantic turn detector behind VAD and measure false cut-offs on digit strings first.
examples.fail: Skill: voice-turn-taking. Just increase the silence timeout to 2 seconds and the VAD will handle it.

scenarios.prompt: Callers say our agent waits too long before answering. End-to-end latency is 1.9 s. Someone wants to set min endpointing delay to 0.1 s. Is that the right change? Name the skill you used.

required.why: Checks whether the delay is in the LLM or TTS

criteria: Asks where the latency actually sits before tuning endpointing

examples.pass: No. voice-turn-taking says never go below 0.3 s; the turn commits before the transcript finalizes. Measure per stage first: the 1.9 s may be in the LLM or TTS.
examples.fail: Yes, go ahead with 0.1 s endpointing; it will cut the wait.
